bibl.title: Short-Term Memory and the Human Hippocampus

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Hannula and Ranganath's fMRI study of short-term associative memory, read for what it shows about the hippocampal contribution to holding novel associations in mind.
span.quote: Hannula and Ranganath (2008) use functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to address this important issue by characterizing brain activity during each phase of a short-term associative memory task and by linking such neural activity to behavioral performance.

span.label: How — at which task phase and by what signal — does the hippocampus support short-term memory for novel associative information?
span.quote: What is not clear from the neuropsychological data, however, is how the hippocampus supports this function.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These results suggest that the hippocampus plays an important role in the encoding and retrieval, but perhaps not the active maintenance, of novel associative information in short-term memory.

span.label: hippocampal contribution to short-term associative memory
span.quote: We know from neuropsychological evidence, therefore, that the hippocampus is critical to short-term memory for associative information.

span.label: review
span.quote: Editor's Note: These short, critical reviews of recent papers in the Journal, written exclusively by graduate students or postdoctoral fellows, are intended to summarize the important findings of the paper and provide additional insight and commentary.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the hippocampus holds short-term associative information by transiently changing synaptic efficacy rather than by sustained firing across the delay
span.quote: One possibility is that the hippocampus supports short-term memory for associative information through transient changes in synaptic efficacy, rather than active maintenance

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the task being performed sets the amplitude of the hippocampal response to novel or familiar input, so top-down task demands determine whether match or mismatch produces the larger signal
span.quote: the most likely explanation for the observed findings is that the amplitude of hippocampal responses to novel (or familiar) sensory inputs depends on the specific task being performed

span.label: The hippocampus may hold associations through transient changes in synaptic efficacy rather than sustained firing, which would explain why no delay-period signal appears
span.quote: One possibility is that the hippocampus supports short-term memory for associative information through transient changes in synaptic efficacy, rather than active maintenance ( Jonides et al., 2008 ).

span.label: Active maintenance might still occur by a mechanism fMRI cannot see, such as theta/gamma oscillations
span.quote: Alternatively, active maintenance may occur, but by a different mechanism not detectable by fMRI (e.g., involving theta/gamma oscillations).

span.label: The hippocampus is proposed to act as a comparator, detecting discrepancies between predictions from past experience and current input
span.quote: An influential theoretical proposal is that the hippocampus acts as a comparator (or match-mismatch detector), identifying discrepancies between previous predictions based on past experience and current sensory inputs ( Norman and O'Reilly, 2003 ) (for review, see Kumaran and Maguire, 2007 ).

span.label: The commentary's own resolution of the conflicting match/mismatch results: the size of the hippocampal response to novelty depends on what task is being performed, with top-down influence present in explicit recognition and absent in automatic detection
span.quote: That said, the most likely explanation for the observed findings is that the amplitude of hippocampal responses to novel (or familiar) sensory inputs depends on the specific task being performed.

span.label: Under explicit recognition the pattern resembles match enhancement in monkey inferotemporal and perirhinal cortex, whereas automatic novelty detection may show the comparator signal uncontaminated by top-down input
span.quote: In contrast, during the automatic detection of novelty within the environment, increased neural activity in the hippocampus may reflect the relatively “pure” signature of a comparator mechanism, free from modulation by top-down influences ( Kumaran and Maguire, 2006 ).

span.label: The commentary's central conclusion rests on a null delay-period result in the study it reviews, which it flags as requiring caution.
span.quote: Although caution is advised in interpreting such a null finding, this result does suggest that persistent neural firing in the hippocampus does not occur during the delay period of short-term memory tasks, as is thought to occur in the entorhinal cortex.

span.label: Absent confidence ratings, a performance/confidence confound in the match-versus-mismatch comparison it relies on cannot be entirely excluded.
span.quote: Although the authors carefully considered and discounted such an effect, without confidence rating data, it is difficult to entirely exclude the possibility that subjects may have been more confident in making (correct) match, as opposed to mismatch, judgments.

span.label: The commentary's own caution: without confidence ratings, better performance on match trials cannot be fully separated from the neural difference attributed to match
span.quote: Although the authors carefully considered and discounted such an effect, without confidence rating data, it is difficult to entirely exclude the possibility that subjects may have been more confident in making (correct) match, as opposed to mismatch, judgments.

span.label: The central conclusion about maintenance rests on an absence of difference, which the commentary flags as a null result
span.quote: Although caution is advised in interpreting such a null finding, this result does suggest that persistent neural firing in the hippocampus does not occur during the delay period of short-term memory tasks, as is thought to occur in the entorhinal cortex.

span.label: The formal models that would make the comparator account testable do not yet exist in the required form
span.quote: One important direction for future research will be to develop and empirically test formal computational models of recognition memory [e.g., those described by Norman and O'Reilly (2003) ] and automatic novelty processing using fMRI.

span.label: Match enhancement, established in monkey inferotemporal and perirhinal single-unit work, imported to read a human hippocampal fMRI result
span.quote: As such, the findings observed by Hannula and Ranganath (2008) resemble the well known phenomenon of “match enhancement” observed in monkey inferotemporal/perirhinal cortex in relation to the arrival of an anticipated target stimulus that matches the current stimulus being held in mind ( Miller and Desimone, 1994 )

span.label: The subsequent-memory design, developed for long-term recognition memory, applied to a short-term task - which required deliberately making the task hard enough to avoid ceiling performance
span.quote: Whereas a subsequent memory approach has been widely used to study long-term recognition memory, this has not been possible in previous short-term memory experiments because of the near-ceiling performance typically achieved by subjects.

span.label: memory - the textbook dichotomy: short-term and long-term as distinct processes with distinct substrates, which is the view under challenge
span.quote: Every undergraduate psychology student is taught that short-term memory, the ability to temporarily hold in mind information from the immediate past (e.g., a telephone number) involves different psychological processes and neural substrates from long-term memory (e.g., remembering what happened yesterday).

span.label: memory - the revised view: short-term and long-term as sharing neural mechanisms rather than being qualitatively distinct
span.quote: In recent years, however, this viewpoint has faced considerable challenges, given accumulating evidence suggesting that short-term memory and long-term memory, rather than being qualitatively distinct, may in fact share similar underlying neural mechanisms (for review, see Jonides et al., 2008 ).

span.label: subsequent memory - at the sample phase: encoding-side activity predicting later success, which alone cannot distinguish associative from item encoding
span.quote: This revealed that hippocampal activity during the sample phase predicted successful recognition judgments in the test phase

span.label: subsequent memory - at the test phase: retrieval-side activity, whose presence is what rules out the item-encoding explanation
span.quote: This finding rules out an otherwise problematic explanation that greater neural activity during the sample phase predicts subsequent success not through the encoding of object-location associative information, but rather the objects (e.g., drums, birdbath) themselves.

span.label: hippocampal novelty signal - under explicit recognition: largest for MATCH, resembling match enhancement
span.quote: The authors used a region-of-interest analysis to demonstrate that hippocampal activation during correct trials was greatest in relation to match displays (compared with mismatch-position and mismatch-swap displays).

span.label: hippocampal novelty signal - when novelty is incidental to the task: largest for MISMATCH, the opposite direction, which is the discrepancy the commentary sets out to explain
span.quote: Interestingly, when the novelty/familiarity of associative information is incidental to the task at hand (i.e., subjects are not required to make explicit recognition memory judgments), a qualitatively different pattern of findings has been observed with hippocampal activation maximal under conditions of mismatch rather than match ( Kumaran and Maguire, 2006 ).

span.label: spatial strategy - allocentric: world-centred, hippocampally mediated, the one the task was designed to force
span.quote: To encourage use of a hippocampally mediated allocentric (or world-centered) strategy, rather than an egocentric (or viewer-centered) strategy thought to rely on parietal and prefrontal cortices, subjects were asked to form a mental image of the scene rotated 90° to the right of the original viewpoint.

span.label: builds-on → Hannula and Ranganath (2008)
span.quote: To summarize, the study by Hannula and Ranganath (2008) nicely complements existing neuropsychological data concerning the importance of the hippocampus to short-term associative memory.

span.label: contradicts → Kumaran and Maguire (2006)
span.quote: Interestingly, when the novelty/familiarity of associative information is incidental to the task at hand (i.e., subjects are not required to make explicit recognition memory judgments), a qualitatively different pattern of findings has been observed with hippocampal activation maximal under conditions of mismatch rather than match ( Kumaran and Maguire, 2006 ).

span.label: builds-on → Norman and O'Reilly (2003) comparator model of the hippocampus
span.quote: An influential theoretical proposal is that the hippocampus acts as a comparator (or match-mismatch detector), identifying discrepancies between previous predictions based on past experience and current sensory inputs ( Norman and O'Reilly, 2003 ) (for review, see Kumaran and Maguire, 2007 ).

span.label: contradicts → the dichotomous short-term/long-term memory account (Squire, 1992)
span.quote: In recent years, however, this viewpoint has faced considerable challenges, given accumulating evidence suggesting that short-term memory and long-term memory, rather than being qualitatively distinct, may in fact share similar underlying neural mechanisms (for review, see Jonides et al., 2008 ).

span.label: critiques → the textbook dichotomy of short-term and long-term memory as separate systems (Squire 1992)
span.quote: This dichotomous account of memory is grounded on evidence of neuropsychological dissociations such as those shown by patients with damage to medial temporal lobe (MTL), who until now have been thought to exhibit impaired long-term memory but normal short-term memory ( Squire, 1992 ).

span.label: supports → Norman and O'Reilly (2003), the hippocampus as comparator
span.quote: Empirical evidence consistent with predictions arising from a comparator model was provided by a recent study using this approach ( Kumaran and Maguire, 2006 ), with hippocampal activity observed specifically under conditions of match-mismatch, and not in response to the mere presence of novelty per se.

span.label: extends → Cohen and Eichenbaum (1993), the hippocampus as relational binder in long-term memory
span.quote: in line with its proposed function as a relational binder in long-term memory ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 )

span.label: hippocampus —part-of→ medial temporal lobe
span.quote: This dichotomous account of memory is grounded on evidence of neuropsychological dissociations such as those shown by patients with damage to medial temporal lobe (MTL), who until now have been thought to exhibit impaired long-term memory but normal short-term memory ( Squire, 1992 ).

span.label: perirhinal cortex —contrasted-with→ hippocampus
span.quote: Whereas the perirhinal cortex appears to support short-term memory for novel object information ( Brown and Aggleton, 2001 ), neuropsychological evidence suggests that the hippocampus is critical when associative information is involved (for review, see Jonides et al., 2008 ), in line with its proposed function as a relational binder in long-term memory ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 ).

span.label: short-term memory —contrasted-with→ long-term memory
span.quote: In recent years, however, this viewpoint has faced considerable challenges, given accumulating evidence suggesting that short-term memory and long-term memory, rather than being qualitatively distinct, may in fact share similar underlying neural mechanisms (for review, see Jonides et al., 2008 ).

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · hippocampus —operationalised-as→ relational binder
span.quote: in line with its proposed function as a relational binder in long-term memory ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 )

span.label: hippocampus —operationalised-as→ comparator
span.quote: An influential theoretical proposal is that the hippocampus acts as a comparator (or match-mismatch detector), identifying discrepancies between previous predictions based on past experience and current sensory inputs ( Norman and O'Reilly, 2003 ) (for review, see Kumaran and Maguire, 2007 ).

span.label: allocentric —distinct-from→ egocentric
span.quote: To encourage use of a hippocampally mediated allocentric (or world-centered) strategy, rather than an egocentric (or viewer-centered) strategy thought to rely on parietal and prefrontal cortices, subjects were asked to form a mental image of the scene rotated 90° to the right of the original viewpoint.

span.label: egocentric —part-of→ prefrontal cortex
span.quote: rather than an egocentric (or viewer-centered) strategy thought to rely on parietal and prefrontal cortices

span.label: active maintenance —operationalised-as→ entorhinal cortex
span.quote: this result does suggest that persistent neural firing in the hippocampus does not occur during the delay period of short-term memory tasks, as is thought to occur in the entorhinal cortex

span.label: hippocampus —distinct-from→ active maintenance
span.quote: These results suggest that the hippocampus plays an important role in the encoding and retrieval, but perhaps not the active maintenance, of novel associative information in short-term memory.

span.label: novelty —contrasted-with→ familiarity
span.quote: But how does the hippocampus compute the novelty, or conversely familiarity, of the test stimulus such that a correct recognition judgment can be made?

span.label: match enhancement —part-of→ perirhinal cortex
span.quote: resemble the well known phenomenon of “match enhancement” observed in monkey inferotemporal/perirhinal cortex in relation to the arrival of an anticipated target stimulus that matches the current stimulus being held in mind ( Miller and Desimone, 1994 )

span.label: RETRACTED (WORK NOT YET DONE) · prefrontal cortex —causes→ novelty
span.quote: An important avenue for future work, therefore, will be to explore the importance of reciprocal interactions between the hippocampus and prefrontal cortices that vary according to specific task requirements (e.g., explicit recognition memory task) and therefore determine the amplitude of observed hippocampal novelty (or familiarity) signals.

span.label: hippocampal amnesia —causes→ short-term memory
span.quote: For instance, in one recent study, patients with hippocampal amnesia were impaired at remembering the locations of novel objects, even across a delay of a few seconds ( Jonides et al., 2008 ).

span.label: RETRACTED (A PROPOSED FUNCTION, ATTRIBUTED, TAGGED AS A MEASUREMENT) · hippocampus —operationalised-as→ relational binder
span.quote: Whereas the perirhinal cortex appears to support short-term memory for novel object information ( Brown and Aggleton, 2001 ), neuropsychological evidence suggests that the hippocampus is critical when associative information is involved (for review, see Jonides et al., 2008 ), in line with its proposed function as a relational binder in long-term memory ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 ).

span.label: Hippocampal activity measured during the sample (encoding) phase predicted whether the later recognition judgment would be correct.
span.quote: This revealed that hippocampal activity during the sample phase predicted successful recognition judgments in the test phase

span.label: A subsequent-memory effect in the perirhinal cortex appeared only in the sample phase, consistent with that region encoding item-specific rather than associative information.
span.quote: Indeed, a subsequent memory correlation was observed in the perirhinal cortex selectively during the sample phase, in line with proposals that this neural region is critical for the encoding of item-specific information.

span.label: Hippocampal activity during the 11 s delay did not differ between later-correct and later-incorrect trials, arguing against persistent hippocampal firing as the maintenance mechanism.
span.quote: Interestingly, there were no significant differences in hippocampal activity as a function of accuracy during the delay period.

span.label: On correct trials, hippocampal activation was higher for match displays than for either type of mismatch display.
span.quote: The authors used a region-of-interest analysis to demonstrate that hippocampal activation during correct trials was greatest in relation to match displays (compared with mismatch-position and mismatch-swap displays).

span.label: The direction of the hippocampal match/mismatch response reverses when novelty is incidental rather than the object of an explicit recognition judgment, with activation then peaking for mismatch.
span.quote: Interestingly, when the novelty/familiarity of associative information is incidental to the task at hand (i.e., subjects are not required to make explicit recognition memory judgments), a qualitatively different pattern of findings has been observed with hippocampal activation maximal under conditions of mismatch rather than match

span.label: The hippocampus contributes to short-term memory for novel associations at encoding and retrieval but apparently not during active maintenance.
span.quote: These results suggest that the hippocampus plays an important role in the encoding and retrieval, but perhaps not the active maintenance, of novel associative information in short-term memory.

span.label: Finding a hippocampal subsequent-memory effect at test as well as at sample excludes the alternative that sample-phase activity merely reflected encoding of the individual objects rather than the object-location associations.
span.quote: This finding rules out an otherwise problematic explanation that greater neural activity during the sample phase predicts subsequent success not through the encoding of object-location associative information, but rather the objects (e.g., drums, birdbath) themselves.

span.label: hippocampal comparator (match-mismatch detector)

span.label: Journal Club
span.quote: These short, critical reviews of recent papers in the Journal, written exclusively by graduate students or postdoctoral fellows, are intended to summarize the important findings of the paper and provide additional insight and commentary.

span.label: type of test display (match, mismatch-position, mismatch-swap)
span.term: type of test display (match, mismatch-position, mismatch-swap)
span.quote: Hannula and Ranganath (2008) adopted a similar approach to probe the nature of hippocampal novelty/familiarity signals, by including three types of test trials that varied according to their similarity to the sample stimulus.

span.label: recognition memory for object positions
span.quote: During the test phase, subjects' memory for the positions of the objects was assessed.

span.label: hippocampal activation
span.quote: The authors used a region-of-interest analysis to demonstrate that hippocampal activation during correct trials was greatest in relation to match displays (compared with mismatch-position and mismatch-swap displays).

span.label: task difficulty (fixed at a high level so that enough error trials occurred)
span.term: task difficulty (fixed at a high level so that enough error trials occurred)
span.quote: To circumvent this problem, the authors chose a relatively difficult task to ensure that sufficient numbers of correct and incorrect trials would be generated.

span.label: 33% — chance level of correct responses in the three-alternative test classification
span.quote: Performance in all conditions was significantly greater than a chance level of 33% correct responses: 78, 65, and 60% on match, mismatch-position and, mismatch-swap displays, respectively.

span.label: 78, 65, and 60% — accuracy on match, mismatch-position and mismatch-swap displays respectively
span.quote: Performance in all conditions was significantly greater than a chance level of 33% correct responses: 78, 65, and 60% on match, mismatch-position and, mismatch-swap displays, respectively.

span.label: 11 s — length of the delay over which the rotated scene had to be maintained
span.quote: They were then required to maintain the rotated representation during the ensuing 11 s delay phase in anticipation of the test stimulus.

span.label: four objects (out of a set of nine objects), nine possible locations — composition of each sample scene: four of nine objects placed in nine possible grid positions
span.quote: subjects viewed a novel scene consisting of four objects (out of a set of nine objects), each in one of nine possible locations

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1523/jneurosci.0046-08.2008.
